newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks set record closing high, turnover.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks set record closing high, turnover.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index broke more records on Monday as another rally in HSBC Holdings spearheaded a drive to an all-time intra-day high before blue chips settled at a record close on record turnover.
The Hang Seng Index closed 57.00 points, or 0.41 percent, higher at 13,987.80 after surging to an all-time intra-day high of 14,130.07.
Turnover beat Friday's record HK$17.85 billion, rising to a bumper HK$18.04 billion.
"Quite a lot of it is just HSBC driven," said Alan Hutcheson, banking analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Shares in HSBC Holdings Plc jumped to a record high of HK$224.00 before closing the session up HK$1.00 at HK$218.00.
Heavy demand for banking stocks in London boosted the share price, analysts said.

They said record turnover in the Hong Kong market was due to a shift in Asian fund flows into the territory, with investors drawn in by the market's recent stellar performance. "If you want to buy Asia, this is where you buy," said Hutcheson.
U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan had bolstered market sentiment last week by saying he expected economic growth to slow later this year, analysts said.
"Wall Street is strong and the bond market is strong," said Archie Hart, associate director at BZW Asia. "The (local) market seems pretty strong to me and it is going up on big volume."
But Hart said investors were tempted to take profit above 14,000 points. "I think the market will be vulnerable to a bit of profit-taking if it gets much higher," he said.
Shares in Hongkong Telecom jumped HK$0.60 to HK$15.10 following Friday's announcement that CITIC Pacific had agreed to sell its 7.74 percent stake to China Everbright Holdings.
CITIC Pacific gained HK$0.50 to HK$44.90 while the three listed subsidiaries of the China Everbright group also rose.
China Everbright Technology rose HK$0.64 to HK$1.89 and and China Everbright International gained HK$0.13 to HK$2.00. China Everbright-IHD Pacific advanced HK$0.50 to HK$9.30.
"The market seems to be saying that it is good news for CITIC that they sold and good news for China Everbright that they bought," said Hart.
Property stocks underperformed the market on Monday, with Sun Hung Kai Properties falling HK$0.75 to HK$91.00 and Henderson Land finishing down HK$0.50 at HK$70.50.
